# Raw-key authenticated mode: cross-language known-answer vectors

Generated from the Rust reference implementation (`dorado-cli`; raw-key mode
is authenticated by default, these vectors were generated when the mode was
still behind an `--authenticated` opt-in flag), which is the baseline for
these vectors per the top-level `CLAUDE.md`. Every other port's test suite should hardcode these as
known-answer tests: derive the subkeys, encrypt the given plaintext with the
given key/tweak/iv/mac/chunk_size, and confirm the ciphertext matches
byte-for-byte; then decrypt the given ciphertext and confirm the plaintext
matches. This is the raw-key-mode counterpart to the `.mahi` password-container
fixtures already used by each port (see each port's `tests/fixtures/` /
`test/fixtures/` / `src/test/resources/`); raw mode has no self-describing
container, so the parameters are recorded here explicitly instead of being
readable from a header.

The construction itself is specified in [`../spec.md`](../spec.md) under "Raw-key
modes". All values below are hex-encoded, generated with a command of the shape:

```
dorado encrypt --key <key> --iv <iv> --tweak <tweak> \
  --mac <mac> --chunk-kib <chunk_kib> --in plaintext.bin --out ciphertext.bin
```

(authenticated is the default for raw-key mode; `--unauthenticated` selects
bare CTR instead)

## Vector: t256_skein_single

- variant: Threefish-256 (32-byte key/iv)
- mac: skein (Skein-512)
- chunk_kib: 64 (payload fits in a single frame)
- key: `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111`
- iv: `0202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202`
- tweak: `00000000000000000000000000000000`
- plaintext (hex): `65786572636973696e6720746865207261772061757468656e7469636174656420636f6e737472756374696f6e206163726f7373206c616e677561676573`
- ciphertext (hex): `010000003ef672003645a72252f71193824a177172deeb59677ab44c27f9d766e9970fbd3d64035d624cf2ab167e9278595a5fb8f39bbd7e178d5f5e2054d2fc14b8961a7bb9296d0da601e3aba580a70532ad6b83e8fc1050620de95d5ba50e545621`

## Vector: t256_hmac_single

Same key/iv/tweak/plaintext as `t256_skein_single`, MAC swapped to HMAC-SHA256.
Note the ciphertext bytes up to the tag are identical to `t256_skein_single`
(the encryption subkey derivation does not depend on which MAC is later
selected for the tag; only the trailing 32-byte tag differs) — a useful
self-check for a port's implementation.

- mac: hmac-sha256
- chunk_kib: 64
- key: `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111`
- iv: `0202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202`
- tweak: `00000000000000000000000000000000`
- plaintext (hex): `65786572636973696e6720746865207261772061757468656e7469636174656420636f6e737472756374696f6e206163726f7373206c616e677561676573`

## Vector: t256_skein_multichunk

Exercises multiple frames (a 1 KiB chunk size against a payload well over
1 KiB), so a port's implementation must get the continuous counter and
per-frame AAD right across a chunk boundary, not just a single frame.

- variant: Threefish-256
- mac: skein
- chunk_kib: 1
- key: `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111`
- iv: `0202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202020202`
- tweak: `00000000000000000000000000000000`
- plaintext (ASCII, 1414 bytes): `a longer payload meant to span multiple one-kilobyte authenticated chunks so the cross-language fixture also exercises the continuous counter and per-frame tagging across chunk boundaries, not just a single frame. ` followed by 1200 `x` characters.
- plaintext (hex): ``
- ciphertext (hex): ``

## Tamper-detection expectation (no fixed vector, a behavioral requirement)

Every port's test suite should also confirm, using any vector above: flipping
any single byte of the ciphertext (including the tag) before decrypting must
be rejected (an authentication-failure error), never silently accepted or
produced as different plaintext. Likewise, decrypting with the wrong key, the
wrong tweak, or the wrong IV must be rejected — the tweak and IV are bound into
frame 0's AAD (see `../spec.md`), not just used for the keystream, so swapping
either alone (holding ciphertext and tag fixed) must fail rather than produce
different plaintext silently.
